=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1437-1438 and 1446-1447 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `gh_retry gh api ... > "${response_file}" 2>&1` mixes `gh_retry` stderr warnings into the JSON response file, so a successful retry can leave invalid JSON for `jq`.
  WHY: Any stderr output corrupts `.id` parsing, which can trigger recovery paths or leave comment metadata unpersisted and create duplicate comments.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1418-1420 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: When `COMMENTS_FETCH_OK` is false and the stored body hash matches, the helper returns before persisting a missing `completion_status_comment_id`.
  WHY: If the ID was lost earlier, this shortcut can keep the state file unhydrated until a later fetch path repairs it, risking a duplicate POST.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1305-1319 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: The docstring claims the helper never issues a per-cycle list call, but the recovery helper can paginate issue comments to recover a malformed response ID.
  WHY: The comment is outdated and can mislead maintainers about the helper's API cost profile.

  PROBLEM: The docstring claims the helper never issues a per-cycle list call, but the recovery helper can paginate issue comments to recover a malformed response ID.

  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The docstring claims the helper never issues a per-cycle list call, but the recovery helper can paginate issue comments to recover a malformed response ID.
  WHY: The comment is outdated and can mislead maintainers about the helper's API cost profile.
- agents.md:132-154 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The documentation still advertises `<!-- ORCH_STATE_V2_… -->` even though the implementation writes `<!-- ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V2 part=N/N manifest=<sha> -->`.
  WHY: Tooling or operators grepping for the documented prefix will miss the actual state comments, breaking downstream parsing.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1275-1319 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The `STATE_FILE` read-modify-write path for completion-status metadata and alert flags is not protected by locking.
  WHY: Concurrent pollers can overwrite each other's updates, losing the cached comment ID or repeating once-per-project alerts.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1472-1528 and 10190-10192 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: `refresh_validation_dispatch_wave_gate` computes `WAVE_COMPLETE`, `ANY_FAILED`, and `PROJECT_COMPLETE`, but the later wave-status block overwrites those globals from Python JSON.
  WHY: The two paths can present inconsistent status in the same cycle, leading to stale readiness/dispatch decisions.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1458-1462 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The helper persists comment metadata even when the PATCH/POST `gh api` write failed.
  WHY: That can poison the cached hash/comment ID and stop the run from retrying correctly until the next cycle.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:~4701-4724, ~4892-4921, 9138-9145 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: If `refresh_validation_dispatch_wave_gate` returns 1, the caller only logs a warning and continues without any fallback status update path.
  WHY: A transient GraphQL/helper failure can leave the tracker comment showing `ready` while the actual wave status is failed until the next full poll cycle.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:9138-9145 and 10191-10200 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: `refresh_validation_dispatch_wave_gate` writes `WAVE_COMPLETE`, `ANY_FAILED`, and `PROJECT_COMPLETE`, but the later wave-status block overwrites those same globals from Python JSON.
  WHY: The helper and the later decision block can disagree within the same cycle, producing stale or inconsistent readiness state.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1458-1463, 4816, 4862, 4950, ~10037 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The callers wrap `update_completion_status_comment ... || true`, so they cannot react when the helper reports a failed write.
  WHY: The completion-status comment can stay stale and the same write may be retried every poll tick during persistent API failures.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:~4701-4724, ~4892-4921, ~10191 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `refresh_validation_dispatch_wave_gate` recomputes the scratch vars from live data, but the later wave-status block overwrites those same variables unconditionally.
  WHY: The same cycle can show inconsistent status, which can skew the pinned comment and Telegram escalation path.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:10001-10013 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The completion-status body re-parses the same `WAVE_STATUS` JSON through multiple separate `jq` invocations.
  WHY: This is inefficient on the poller's hot path and adds unnecessary subprocess overhead on every cycle.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:~10191-10300 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The new `_csc_*` locals and `COMPLETION_STATUS_STATE_CHANGED` flag are not cleared on every early-return path.
  WHY: A later issue in the same run can inherit stale values and build incorrect completion-status comments or skip validation dispatch.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1437-1438 and 1446-1447 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `gh_retry gh api ... > "${response_file}" 2>&1` redirect captures both stdout and stderr from the `gh_retry` wrapper into the same response file.
  WHY: `gh_retry` emits retry warnings on stderr, so a successful retry can leave the response file containing both warning text and JSON, which breaks `jq` parsing and can lead to duplicate completion-status comments.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1418-1420 | severity=medium | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: When `COMMENTS_FETCH_OK` is `"false"` and `state_hash` matches `body_hash`, the function returns 0 without calling `persist_completion_status_comment_state`.
  WHY: If the state file is missing a valid comment ID, this early return can suppress the later fix-up path and leave the helper prone to duplicate POSTs.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1349-1351 (docstring) vs 1320-1345 (recover_completion_status_comment_id_from_live_comments) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The docstring says "The helper never issues a per-cycle list call on its own," but the recovery helper does exactly that.
  WHY: This is a documentation inconsistency that misstates the helper's API cost profile.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- agents.md:137 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Documentation shows `<!-- ORCH_STATE_V2_… -->` but the actual marker used in the code is `<!-- ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V2 part=N/N manifest=<sha> -->`.
  WHY: Downstream tooling or operators grepping for the documented marker will never find the actual state comments, making the documentation misleading for automation parsing.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1305-1319 (docstring) | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The docstring claims "The helper never issues a per-cycle list call on its own", but `recover_completion_status_comment_id_from_live_comments` makes exactly such a list call when recovering from malformed responses.
  WHY: The documentation contract is outdated and misleads future maintainers about the actual API call behavior.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1275-1310 (persist_completion_status_comment_state) and wave-status block | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: No file locking protects the read-modify-write sequence when persisting `completion_status_comment_id` / `completion_status_comment_body_hash` to STATE_FILE, and similarly for `.completion_status_failure_alert_sent` updates.
  WHY: Concurrent orchestrator instances can race and lose updates, causing duplicate completion-status comments or repeated Telegram alerts.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1472-1528 (refresh_validation_dispatch_wave_gate) vs 10190-10192 (wave-status block) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `refresh_validation_dispatch_wave_gate` computes `WAVE_COMPLETE`, `ANY_FAILED`, `PROJECT_COMPLETE` from live data, but the later wave-status block overwrites these same variables from Python's `check-wave-status` JSON output.
  WHY: A validating project with a newly skipped or implementation-failed sub-issue can dispatch validation or display incorrect "ready" status until the next full poll cycle completes.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1438 and 1447 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Both the PATCH and POST calls to GitHub API redirect both stdout and stderr into the same response file with `> "${response_file}" 2>&1`.
  WHY: If gh emits any warning or progress messages to stderr on a successful call, the JSON parsing via `jq -r '.id // empty'` receives corrupted data.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1418-1420 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When `comments_fetch_ok != "true"` and the hash matches (`state_hash == body_hash`), the function returns early at line 1420 without calling `persist_completion_status_comment_state`.
  WHY: This can leave `state_comment_id` unpersisted if it was previously missing, so later cycles may create duplicate pinned comments once comment fetch becomes available again.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM mistralai_mistral-small-2603 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1438-1468 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: GitHub CLI diagnostics emitted to stderr are captured into `response_file` along with the JSON body.
  WHY: If `gh` writes a warning or progress line on an otherwise-successful call, the file is no longer valid JSON and `response_id` parsing fails, triggering recovery logic or duplicate marker comments.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1418-1420 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The early-return path when `comments_fetch_ok != "true"` and the hash matches does not persist a known-valid comment ID.
  WHY: If the ID was missing or lost earlier, later cycles without comment fetch can remain stuck without a saved ID and may duplicate the completion-status comment when fetch recovers.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1373-1377 (docstring of `update_completion_status_comment`) | severity=low | confidence=1
  PROBLEM: The docstring says "The helper never issues a per-cycle list call on its own," but the fallback recovery path does exactly that.
  WHY: This is a misleading documentation contract for maintainers auditing API usage; it is not a runtime failure.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1458-1462 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The helper
